newsitem.title: JAPAN: ASIAN TRADERS EXPECT LME ALUMINIUM PRICES TO FALL.
newsitem.headline: ASIAN TRADERS EXPECT LME ALUMINIUM PRICES TO FALL.

text.p: Aluminium prices are set to fall further after sharp losses on the London Metal Exchange (LME) overnight, Japanese traders said on Wednesday.
"Aluminium prices are set to dip further, but prices under $1,700 will attract moderate physical buying interest," a trader at a major trading house said.
Traders agreed that a correction was long overdue after a strong rally over the past several days.
"As we have not heard that funds are starting to liquidate their positions, aluminium has more scope to rise again after a technical correction," another trading house trader said.
Traders said during Asian trade, buying interest from Japanese traders was sluggish due to the "Obon" summer holidays.

At 0435 GMT, benchmark three-month aluminium was quoted at $1,715/$1,719 a tonne, down from $1,722/$1,724 at 1800 GMT in London on Tuesday. It had cascaded below $1,700 briefly before finishing the kerb at $1,715, down $35 from the previous day.
Traders expect zinc to move volatilely for some time, although they said sentiment remains bullish.
At 0610 GMT, zinc and copper prices were not quoted. Zinc ended the kerb at $1,480, down $65 from the previous day, and copper at $2,278, up $4.
"LME copper prices are set to fall gradually to around $1,200 although a short-term technical rebound is likely," a copper trader said.
